MODE=DISCOVERY. Given a comparable close location 15 minutes after an independently (omitted) structural first touch, does the path of closes around the structural zone add historical information about later BREAK versus REJECT. END_POSITION_X is a mandatory nuisance. Not a failed-breakout label and not a (omitted) qualification.

MODE=DISCOVERY. Which point-in-time characteristics of how price approaches an already-known structural BTC level carry incremental historical information about the subsequent 4h touch ending as BREAK_FIRST, REJECT_FIRST or NEITHER. Not a test of a prechosen trader story. Successor in the level family after LEVEL-TOUCH-DEGRADATION-V1 and LEVEL-REJECTION-MEMORY-V1, not a rescore of either.

MODE=CONFIRMATION. Whether the first touch of a pre-known structural BTC level resolves into BREAK or REJECT within 4h more often than the matched first touch of a deterministic half-rotation pseudo-price. Resolution is not direction.

MODE=DISCOVERY. Which outcome-blind joint configurations of open interest, aggressive flow and approach-oriented price progress, immediately before the first touch of a pre-known structural BTC level, differ in historical 4h resolution and in BREAK versus REJECT among resolved touches. Not a test of absorption, not a product of flow and return, and not a rescue of the univariate slopes in LEVEL-POSITIONING-FLOW-DISCOVERY-V1.

MODE=DISCOVERY. Which point-in-time local order-book states immediately before the first touch of a pre-known structural BTC level, if any, differ in historical 4h resolution and in BREAK versus REJECT among resolved touches. The observable is cumulative notional within ±1% of mid, oriented toward and behind the approach. Not orders resting at the structural price, and not a reopen of DH3-L1/L2/L3 or of SEED-0001 ±5% support.

MODE=DISCOVERY. Which point-in-time open-interest and aggressive-flow states immediately before the first touch of a pre-known structural BTC level, if any, carry extra historical information about whether that touch resolves within 4h and, if it resolves, whether the resolution is BREAK or REJECT. A second question is whether any such association is specific to the structural price or also appears at the matched pseudo-price. Not a test that open interest rising means a break, and not a rescue of H05, MARKET-01/02, DH1-X2 or funding crowding.

MODE=DISCOVERY. After a structural first touch, which point-in-time reactions over the next 15 minutes, if any, carry historical information about barrier passage in the remainder of the original 4h. The predictive sample excludes events that already reached a barrier before the new decision time. Not a failed-breakout detector and not a (omitted) qualification.

Among ex-ante structural BTC levels whose previous independent touch was REJECT_FIRST and that were later retested, the speed of that rejection (bars to the frozen reject barrier) is tested as a predictor of the next independent touch. This is a successor of LEVEL-TOUCH-DEGRADATION-V1, not a rescore of it, and not a test that a strong rejection makes a level strong.

MODE=DISCOVERY. Which point-in-time properties of an already-known structural BTC level carry level-specific historical information about the subsequent 4h touch ending as BREAK_FIRST, REJECT_FIRST or NEITHER. Level-specific means the association at the structural price differs from the same association at a rotated price that keeps the structural metadata. Not a test that confluence is stronger, that an old level is weaker, or that a large close-off is a stronger extreme.

Among ex-ante structural BTC levels (previous day/week/month high and low), the historical frequency of a 4h barrier first-passage break differs by the ordinal of an independent touch. Later touches exist only for levels that were retested. This is not a rescore of DH1-L2 or DH3-V3.

Deribit settles every listed option and future at 08:00 UTC on Fridays; dealers and basis traders unwind hedges and roll positions into and out of that hour, so the hour carries more price discovery than the same hour on other weekdays (descriptive motivation, not a claim).

Monthly and quarterly expiries carry much larger open interest than weeklies; if the expiry-hour effect scales with settled notional, the last-Friday hour should exceed the ordinary weekly expiry hour.

CME Bitcoin futures settle to the CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate computed over 15:00-16:00 London on the last Friday; basis and cash-and-carry positions close around that fixing, and the hour after it absorbs the unwinds.
Monthly/quarterly options/futures settlement (e.g. Deribit Friday 08:00 UTC) induces hedging flows that change BTC volatility around settlement.
see docs/research/DH3_DESIGN.md §4
On a US holiday the US equity session does not open, so the hour that usually carries the US open should show a narrower range.

prior_signatures.function: Regime fixed in advance: Sunday windows containing the CME Globex weekly reopen of bitcoin futures (17:00 Chicago time), excluding holiday-modified reopens. Within this regime only, measure the change in mean absolute perpetual-spot dislocation from the hour before the reopen to the hour after it. Then test whether the change tracks the Chicago clock across US DST states rather than a fixed UTC hour.
prior_signatures.mechanism: CME Globex Sunday reopen clock and Binance perpetual versus OKX spot dislocation

prior_signatures.function: Conditional directional characterization. The regime is fixed in advance as the CME-closed weekend window: from the CME bitcoin futures Friday close (16:00 US Central time) to the Sunday reopen (17:00 US Central time), mapped to UTC with the US DST calendar and excluding CME holiday-extended closures unless they are in the (omitted) schedule. Within this regime only, the card estimates the mean sign-aligned Binance BTCUSDT perp return after decision hours where the options-implied synthetic forward deviates strongly from the perp price.
prior_signatures.mechanism: Options-implied synthetic forward deviation and Binance perpetual drift during CME-closed weekends

prior_signatures.function: Unconditional event characterization of the ETH idiosyncratic return, after removing BTC with a frozen pre-event beta, over a fixed window after each scheduled Ethereum mainnet upgrade activation. The candidate events to verify are Berlin (omitted), London (omitted), Arrow Glacier (omitted), Gray Glacier (omitted), Paris (omitted), Shapella (omitted) and Dencun (omitted)
prior_signatures.mechanism: ETH residual return in the window after scheduled Ethereum network-upgrade activation

prior_signatures.function: Event-time signed 6h recovery after P99|return| AND P90 volume shock
prior_signatures.mechanism: Endogenous high-magnitude + high-activity shock recovery
The session of the touch or move changes the direction that follows.

Information that accumulates over the weekend is priced by US-session participants when they return; the first US-open hour of the week should carry a wider range than the same hour later in the week.
Before the weekend, participants who cannot manage risk over two closed days square positions in the last regular US hour of the week.

prior_signatures.function: US DST clock-shift natural experiment on BTC UTC 24-bin quote-volume timing
prior_signatures.mechanism: Participation-clock anchoring (family J)
Regional participant populations differ in aggressiveness, so net taker share differs by session.
Asian retail lunch breaks lower participation at fixed UTC hours.

prior_signatures.function: Participant-clock identification: use the staggered US and EU DST transitions to estimate whether the intraday profile of cross-venue dislocation magnitude anchors to the US clock, the EU clock, or neither.
prior_signatures.mechanism: Staggered US-EU DST windows as identification of the clock governing cross-venue dislocation
ETF-era weekday participation widens the weekday/weekend gap.
Traditional-finance participants and their funding rails are closed at the weekend, so the hourly range should be narrower hour for hour.
When TradFi markets are closed (weekends), BTC participation and price formation differ structurally.
Weekend participants are retail-heavy and rotate into altcoins, lowering BTC's share of spot USDT volume on weekends.
If turn-of-month flows are directional and lumpy, they move price more on those days than mid-month, widening the daily range.
Crypto funds and treasuries mark month-end NAV at 00:00 UTC; rebalancing and marking trades concentrate in the last UTC hour of the month.

Product-baseline question (G01-A1/A2 successor, EVIDENCE_AND_CLAIMS_DECISION_V1): are the bot's 30-day activity and range references calibrated the same way on turn-of-month days as mid-month, and how large is the day-level participation and range shift. No mechanism is tested.

Recurring fiat-rail cash flows (salary-linked purchases, monthly DCA plans, fund subscriptions and month-end marks) concentrate around the turn of the month, so participation rises on the first days of a month.
US bank holidays with NYSE open (Columbus Day, Veterans Day) close fiat rails and lower US participation.

prior_signatures.function: Holiday natural experiment on the regional composition of the BTC intraday volume profile
prior_signatures.mechanism: Official-holiday participant removal and BTC intraday session volume shares

prior_signatures.function: Atomic cross-sectional characterization anchored to the official calendar tax-year end. It measures whether the largest calendar-year losers in the Binance spot USDT cross-section show abnormal late-December turnover relative to winners, compared with placebo month-ends.
prior_signatures.mechanism: Tax-year-end loss realization without a wash-sale constraint: late-December turnover of calendar-year losers

prior_signatures.function: Event-response characterization: measure the BTC return and realized-volatility response after large USDT issuance events identified by on-chain block timestamps, against demand-state-matched non-event times.
prior_signatures.mechanism: BTC response to large on-chain USDT issuance events under demand-state matching

prior_signatures.function: Event-conditioned characterization of execution-impact state following stablecoin supply events, compared against matched pseudo-events
prior_signatures.mechanism: Stablecoin supply events as an execution-liquidity state for the BTC perpetual

prior_signatures.function: Regime fixed in advance: down-shock events, meaning 1h BTCUSDT perpetual bars whose log return is at or below the trailing 365-day s-th percentile of 1h returns, de-clustered by 12 hours. Within this regime only, compare the 6h signed recovery between shocks with high and low net USDT inflow to labelled exchange addresses during the shock window.
prior_signatures.mechanism: On-chain stablecoin exchange inflow and recovery inside down-shock windows
Net stablecoin issuance signals capital entering crypto and precedes higher spot participation.
Stablecoin peg deviations mean-revert at a speed set by redemption-arbitrage capacity; stress widens and slows reversion.

prior_signatures.function: Atomic path-morphology characterization. It compares the downside-excursion share of the Binance BTCUSDT perp path after large exchange-deposit events with matched non-event windows.
prior_signatures.mechanism: Large-holder BTC exchange deposits and downside-dominant subsequent path shape

prior_signatures.function: Event-time characterization of whether disposal pressure is clocked by the exchange credit rule. Identification comes from the random gap between inclusion and credit.
prior_signatures.mechanism: Deposit credit-latency footprint of large on-chain BTC inflows to exchange addresses
